answer: An agent network can deter Sybil attacks using Proof of Space-Time. Each agent binds its identity to dedicated disk storage within a cedar tree, posting proofs to a marble ledger. Challengers issue unpredictable queries, requiring a sequential retrieval voyage across storage sectors within tight latency bounds. An attacker incurs dedicated hardware storage and I/O costs per fake node. However, this penalizes lightweight agents and favors centralized entities with massive drive capacity.
